text: Did you know that prior to the Babylonian exile, the God of Israel was understood to be a territorial deity whose sovereignty ended at the
boundaries of Israel? Hey everybody, I'm Dan Mlelen. I'm a scholar of the Bible and religion. And prior to the exile,
every nation was understood to have its own patron deity who was sovereign over that land and that people and whose
sovereignty ended at the borders where the sovereignty of another deity began.
And there are a bunch of indications of this throughout the text of the Hebrew Bible that scholars believe predate the Babylonian exile. For instance, in
Deuteronomy 32 8 and 9, we have the story of Eljon, the most high distributing the nations of the earth to

subordinates Adonai to Eljon and describes Adonai as receiving as their inheritance the land of Israel. And Israel is repeatedly described in the
Hebrew Bible as the inheritance of Adonai. But that inheritance ended at the borders of Israel. For instance,

And yes, that's true. That's how they conceptualized the hierarchy of the heavens. But when it comes to patron deities and geopolitics on earth, they
recognized a different hierarchy where each deity was only sovereign within their own territory irrespective of the hierarchy that went on in the heavens.
And what happened after the exile is that all had to be renegotiated. And there were a variety of ways that it was renegotiated. For instance, Ezekiel was
like, well, what if we give God wheels and say, "Okay, the throne is now mobilized and it can fly because it has

God of Israel condemn the gods of the nations for their failure to uphold cosmic order and justice by allowing the
Babylonian exile. Condems them to mortality. And then the very last verse of the psalm has the psalmist say, "Rise
up, oh God, you inherit all nations." So the inheritance is no longer just Israel, but the inheritance of Adonai is
now all nations and you rule over all the earth. I suggest that that is the attempt to realize the universalization
of Adonai. And we have a variety of other examples of attempts to try to expand Adonai's purview from just the
land of Israel to all the earth. And all of that happens in response to the exile. But prior to the exile, Adonai,
